plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial with dense, layered flower heads in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It is a staple of autumn gardens and is cultivated widely for cut flowers and potted displays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; originated in China and widely grown in Japan, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants that set buds as nights lengthen. Japan's Imperial family uses a 16-petal chrysanthemum as its emblem.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall native perennial of North American meadows and roadsides with clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators, including migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in moist meadows, prairies, and roadsides
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies migrating south in October depend heavily on its nectar to fuel their journey to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in sprays of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring, whole streets are carpeted in fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 trees, and a local superstition says a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare stalks topped by umbels of frilly, sparkling pink flowers well after most garden plants have faded. It thrives in sunny, well-drained sites and often flowers in the dry warmth of autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (October to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Drakensberg mountains; grown in gardens of the UK, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The petals have a glittering, crystalline sheen, which gives some nerines the name 'Guernsey lily' and a reputation for sparkling in sunlight.
